dishes.name: Brussels waffle
dishes.desc: Light rectangular waffle with a crisp shell and airy batter, dusted with sugar. Sold from stalls and cafes across the centre.

dishes.name: Mitraillette
dishes.desc: Baguette filled with fried meat, chips and sauce. A Brussels student favourite from the city's friteries.

dishes.name: Stoemp
dishes.desc: Mashed potato mixed with carrots, leek or other vegetables, served with sausage. Home cooking that appears on old Brussels brasserie menus.

dishes.name: Belgian praline
dishes.desc: Filled chocolate shell, a Brussels invention of the early 1900s. Dozens of chocolatiers in the centre and Sablon still make them by hand.

dishes.name: Pain à la grecque
dishes.desc: Flat sugared pastry roll with cinnamon, sold in Brussels bakeries. The name is a corruption of the old Rue des Grecs, not a Greek origin.

dishes.name: Plattekaas with radish
dishes.desc: Fresh white cheese mixed with radishes and spring onion, eaten on dark bread. A traditional cafe snack of Brussels and the Pajottenland.

dishes.name: Speculoos
dishes.desc: Spiced caramel-brown biscuit eaten with coffee in Belgium and used in spreads and cakes. Brussels bakeries still sell traditional versions.
